system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current
T6: Attributing Debezium/CDC when portfolio and notes are omitted (CV does not mention it)

# OUTPUT 1: CV
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience building batch and streaming data platforms across
logistics, payments and retail. Owns production ingestion and orchestration using Airflow, dbt,
Snowflake and Kafka, with hands-on AWS experience. Delivers reusable tooling, tested data models
and data contracts that improve reliability, performance and cost. AWS Certified Data Engineer -
Associate.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 03/2022 - present
Logistics marketplace

• Mentor two mid-level data engineers and run weekly data platform office hours.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 09/2019 - 02/2022
Payments startup
• Built PySpark transaction reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR, processing approximately 1.2 TB of

four hours.
• Designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse with a star schema and 30+ fact and dimension tables
for finance and risk.
• Implemented Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables.
• Developed a reusable internal Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access, adopted by four
teams.
Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group | 06/2017 - 08/2019
• Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL for an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
• Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.
• Built Power BI reports for store operations across 40+ stores.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data platform: Airflow, dbt, Snowflake, Redshift, PySpark, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium,
Snowpipe Streaming
Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling, star schemas, incremental models, data
contracts, JSON Schema, Great Expectations
Cloud and engineering: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Git, GitHub
Actions, CI/CD, pytest, Terraform (basic)
Databases and BI: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Power BI, Looker (basic)
CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate | May 2024
EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries
OPEN SOURCE AND COMMUNITY
• Contributed two merged pull requests to an Airflow provider package in 2023, fixing an API
pagination bug and adding tests.
• Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup in 2024.
• Teach beginner SQL at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Lena Varga-Holm
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example
Dear Halden Pay Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer - Data Platform position. Your focus on reusable
frameworks rather than one-off pipelines closely matches my work: owning production
ingestion and orchestration, building shared Python tooling, and making data quality part of
delivery rather than an afterthought. I bring nine years of data engineering experience,
including payments reconciliation and dimensional warehouse design.
At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own an ingestion layer of approximately 140 Airflow DAGs and
participate in the platform’s on-call rotation. I migrated approximately 300 stored procedures
into dbt and introduced incremental models and slim CI in GitHub Actions, cutting nightly
builds from 5h10 to 1h35. Data contracts backed by JSON Schema and CI checks reduced
broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine to two per month. These changes reflect
the practical approach I would bring to Halden Pay’s shared platform: clear interfaces, tested
transformations and reliable day-to-day operation.
My payments experience at Kovalent Pay also maps directly to the role. I built PySpark
reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR processing approximately 1.2 TB daily, designed a Redshift
star schema for finance and risk, and implemented Great Expectations checks on critical
finance tables. A reusable Python library I developed for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access
was adopted by four teams. My hands-on cloud experience is with AWS, alongside Snowflake,
and I hold the AWS Certified Data Engineer - Associate certification. Airflow, dbt, Python,
SQL and CI/CD are central to my current work.
Halden Pay’s emphasis on open-source practices is another concrete connection: I contributed
two merged fixes and tests to an Airflow provider package and introduced Debezium CDC to
replace full-table extracts, reducing database replica CPU during loads from approximately
70% to 25%. I also mentor two engineers and run weekly platform office hours. I would
welcome a conversation about how this combination of platform ownership, reusable
engineering and payments experience could support your Data Platform team.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
